prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer through screening/sorting/reconciliation/staging to aircraft-loading handoff; excludes loading beyond outbound load-control point. Objectives: safety/accuracy/throughput/cutoff delivery. No explicit modes. Elements/items (recipients unspecified): Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records acceptance/initiates processing/sends Oversize Exception Ticket; Bag Tag Printer produces unique durable passenger/flight-linked tags and required Calibration Witness Tag; Transfer Bag Feeder records inbound bags/sends Late Transfer Bag Card/holds release pending screening/onward-handling confirmation; Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) supplies flight/routing records/sends Flight Cutoff Advisory. Baggage Control System (Velvet) coordinates status/routing/visibility; validates acceptance/records/transfer routing; applies approved screening profiles; loads approved time-effective sort plan, checks flight/handling records before routing exceptions to Secondary Inspection Chute, segregated from outbound flows. Chute/work-area access requires authorized duties. Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) coordinates conveyor availability/active plan; produces Recovery Route Card; permits induction under equipment restrictions. Induction Tray Conveyor controls spacing/identification before routing; interlocks stop feeds for jams/open doors/downstream unreadiness. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel) and South Gate Scanner verify decision-point identities/acquire images/return dispositions; latter supplies independent path reads/Manual Rescan Receipt. Record quality/alarms; incomplete examinations never clear. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) preserves identity/applies destination/screening status; sends Chute Occupancy Note near configured capacity. Prefer approved capacity/time-sufficient paths; prohibit blocked/unavailable releases. Image Resolution Desk staff resolve failures with images/identity/prompts and record dispositions. Pending/alarmed/missing-record bags require examination/control, never make-up; return requires authorized disposition and consistent identity/outcome/routing. Bag Reconciliation Station matches bag/screening record. East Make-Up Conveyor; West Make-Up Conveyor convey toward loading. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) stages only valid-disposition/authorized-route bags. Outbound Load Control Desk confirms readiness. Airline Ramp Coordinator accepts handoff/sends Carousel Release Slip upon authorization. Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates recovery/readiness/staffing/lane-operation; notify for isolation. Security Duty Manager handles nonroutine security decisions; Maintenance Technician supports recovery. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) handles escalated alarms/safety-controls with airport security personnel; inspection staff secure/control isolated bags. Acceptance/transfer require

New part:
S088: A scan mismatch prevents the bag from continuing on a route that depends on the unresolved identity.
S089: Congestion awareness uses current lane availability, conveyor stops, and the observed rate of incoming bags.
S090: The Baggage Operations Supervisor sets local congestion thresholds and confirms the authorized response to sustained overload.
S091: Tern is the operational alias used for the Baggage Operations Supervisor in sortation coordination.
S092: When a planned lane is unavailable, the Baggage Control System selects an approved alternate route only if screening status and flight timing remain valid.
S093: Bags with an unresolved destination or a route outside their handling limits are diverted to the Secondary Inspection Chute.
S094: The Image Resolution Desk resolves image-related holds before affected bags are returned to normal sortation.
S095: The Explosives Response Team manages security holds under the applicable response procedures.
S096: A bag returns to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization agree.
S097: The East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor are selected according to the active plan and available capacity.
S098: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit operates within its assigned flight window and reports when its usable capacity is constrained.
S099: The Transfer Bag Feeder continues to hold transfer bags until screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S100: The Bag Reconciliation Station compares bag identity with the active handling record and flags unresolved discrepancies.
S101: The Bag Reconciliation Station sends a Bag Match Query when bag identity cannot be reconciled with the active handling record.
S102: Bags found on a stopped or misdirected path are held from onward movement until their location and identity are established.
S103: The Maintenance Technician isolates a failed conveyor section and confirms that the route is safe before service resumes.
S104: The Baggage Operations Supervisor authorizes recovery to the approved sort plan after the cause of the abnormal path has been addressed.
S105: Flight Data Gateway maintains scheduled flight identifiers, destinations, planned departure times, and revisions needed for baggage planning.
S106: Flight schedules include airline-specific dispatch targets and connection windows, and changes are time-stamped for operational use.
S107: Baggage Control System evaluates flight assignments against current schedule data before accepting bag routing instructions.
S108: The planned dispatch time is the reference for prioritizing bags, while the published departure time remains the passenger-facing schedule value.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
